title: "11 · From Cogwheels to Words"
---

::: {.milestone}
**Block 4** · the wrap-up. Read this even if you are behind
:::

Step back and admire your script: it opens a window, presents randomised stimuli, restricts and records responses, evaluates them against a rule, and gives feedback. That is a genuine behavioural experiment, and its *skeleton* (setup → trial loop → shutdown) is shared by essentially every paradigm in cognitive science.

Now, CogComm asks how people process *language* in real time. So consider a thought experiment: what if the stimulus were not a cogwheel image but a **word** — and the measure were not accuracy, but *how long you look at the word before pressing on*? If a word is surprising or hard to process, you slow down, and your experiment can see it. That paradigm is called **self-paced reading**, and here is the punchline: your Exercise 5 script is already about 80% of it.

|  | Today: CogWheel | Session 3: self-paced reading |
|---|---|---|
| **Stimuli** | images (`ImageStim`) | words, one at a time (`TextStim`) |
| **Response** | left / right arrows | spacebar |
| **Measure** | accuracy | reading time per word (RT) |
| **Pacing** | participant presses to advance | identical — press to advance! |

::: {.callout-note .predict icon="false" title="🔮 One last prediction"}
Which Session-1 string function turns `'The peanut was salted'` into a list you can loop over, one word at a time?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Check your prediction"}
`.split()` — `'The peanut was salted'.split()` gives `['The', 'peanut', 'was', 'salted']`. The reading loop is then: for each word, `TextStim`, draw, flip, `waitKeys(keyList=['space'])`. Same skeleton. Swap the parts. Session 3 adds the crucial missing pieces: a clock to measure how long each word stayed on screen, and a logfile to save it all.
:::
:::

## Before next session

- **Finish Exercise 5** if you did not get all the way, and keep both scripts safe: Session 3 extends them directly into the Portfolio 2 prototype.
- **Re-run your script and change one thing on purpose** (a colour, a key, the feedback duration). Predict what will happen before you run it.
- Optionally, skim the PsychoPy chapters of the [Programming Experiments in Python and PsychoPy3](https://kristiantylen.gitbooks.io/programming-experiments-in-python-and-psychopy3/content/) gitbook, and keep [psychopy.org](https://psychopy.org/documentation.html) and [learnpython.org](https://www.learnpython.org/) bookmarked.
- **Bring questions** — broken scripts very welcome.

Say it once more with feeling: *prepare, draw, flip, wait.* See you in Session 3.
